messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Azure GermanyNorth control-plane anomalies detected. Increased route churn observed on private peering interfaces affecting on-prem connected Private deployments. Symptoms: intermittent packet loss to private endpoints, high TCP retransmits, customers reporting timeouts. Pager auto-trig: severity=P1 if >2 customers or >10% error rate on routed traffic. Links: https://status.azure.com/incident/xxxxx (detected), https://internal.ops/telemetry/route-churn/gnorth
Priya: taking pager. oncall Priya now. @Jamal can you pull customer impact (CVs) and list impacted Dedicated/Private deployments?
Jamal: looking. Initial check - two Private customers with vWANs (cust-acme, cust-vela) showing intermittent connectivity since ~2350012200. Telemetry shows BGP withdraws and re-announces on MS edge. Packet loss spikes ~30s every 2-3mins.
Rachel: cust-acme support thread: "services in germanynorth failing every few mins, affects webhooks and private db connections". CS alerted and put on-hold for mitigation updates.
Priya: quick triage checklist: 1) confirm route withdraw frequency, 2) check Azure Control Plane incidents, 3) attempt regional reroute -> failover to neighboring region (weurope) for critical prefixes, 4) notify customers and schedule maintenance if needed.
Luca: I see correlated spikes on border NVAs too. Looks like Azure edge is flapping a set of aggregated routes. Possible community tag mis-propagation between peering fabric and our gateways.
Alice: starting quick checks. Running effective route table for NICs in affected subnets: ```bash az network nic show-effective-route-table --resource-group rg-private-cust-acme --name nic-db-02``` returns repeated withdraws for 10.240.0.0/16 at 2350012195,2350012258,2350012350.
Jamal: dumping BGP sessions on our side: ```show ip bgp summary | include 10.240.0.0``` -> bgp session to az-gw1 toggled 3x in last 15m. Not seeing local config change.
SRE-Oncall: echoing -- I've escalated to Azure TAC, they confirm control-plane instability in GermanyNorth affecting route distribution between their edge routers and customer VNets. They're investigating fabric controller churn.
Priya: ok, mitigation path: 1) steer critical customer prefixes to west europe via policy-based export (temporary announcement from our west-europe eBGP peers), 2) apply route dampening on our eBGP adjacency for germanynorth to avoid transient withdraw oscillations propagating to customers, 3) coordinate with Azure TAC for fix ETA. Any objections?
Luca: agree. Steering note: we'll origination more-specific /24s from W-Europe to attract traffic for db host ranges. Need approval to modify eBGP advertisements.
Alice: preparing commands to inject more-specifics for ACME: ```# announce /24s for critical hosts
sudo birdc configure add route 10.240.1.0/24 via 203.0.113.45
# or on our infra
ip route add 10.240.1.0/24 via 203.0.113.45
``` Use with care.
Priya: Jamal and Luca please run the steer and route-damp steps and report back. I'll update customers and post to #customer-notifications.
Jamal: applying dampening on peering: ```sudo birdc set-policy dampen germanynorth-peer half-life=900 suppress=60 reuse=30``` -> applied. Monitoring.
(react: :eyes: )
Luca: injecting more-specifics now for two critical /24s (cust-acme db + cust-vela api).```bash
# orchestration run
orchestrator run --env prod --task inject-prefixes --prefixes 10.240.1.0/24,10.240.2.0/24 --origin weurope
``` Deployed, watching BGP tables.
Alice: telemetry shows traffic for those prefixes shifting to weurope within 40s. Loss reduces to <2% for the test flows. 
Priya: great. Can we keep dampening and more-specifics for next 2 hours while Azure TAC works fix? Need to ensure no collateral impact to other customers.
Luca: adding temporary filter to prevent propagation of these more-specifics to other backbone peers. Limited to targeted eBGP sessions.
SRE-Oncall: Azure TAC gave preliminary root-cause: control-plane reconvergence bug after recent edge fabric update. They're rolling back to a stable config in stages; ETA 90 mins for wide rollbacks, 20-30 mins for partial mitigation in affected fabric.
Priya: update status page and #customer-notifications with short note: "We are mitigating intermittent connectivity issues in Azure GermanyNorth for Private deployments by temporarily steering traffic to West Europe; customers may see traffic routed via W-Europe with slightly higher latency. Azure engineering is rolling a fix." Rachel please send to affected CS threads.
Rachel: notified both customers. ACME set to failover; they asked for timeline and whether IP addresses change. I told them IPs remain same; path changes. They're okay for now.
Jamal: monitoring: BGP oscillation count down from 12->4 in last 10 minutes. Our dampening suppressed noisy withdraws; steady state improving.
Alice: capturing diagnostic snapshot for postmortem: ```
# sample BGP dump
bgpdump -m /var/log/bgp/updates.log | grep "GermanyNorth" > /tmp/gnorth-bgp-flap.log
``` saved.
(react: :white_check_mark: )
SRE-Oncall: raising incident bridge for timeline and RCA: https://meet.prod/bridge/incident-2350012345 at 2350012800.
Priya: handing to follow-up SRE rotation after stabilization window. I'm staying on until Azure marks fabric healthy. If we see re-emergence, re-open pager.
Luca: leaving a TODO: revert more-specifics & dampening after Azure fix validation. I'll create a safe revert job with canary checks.
Jamal: currently traffic % via weurope for affected prefixes: 82% -> 100% for those host prefixes. No new customer errors reported in last 6 minutes.
Rachel: CS confirmed ACME and Vela ack'd update and are monitoring. No business-impact alerts from them.
Priya: incident severity downgraded to SEV2 at 2350013000 as customer-facing errors reduced, but we keep status page and mitigation in place until Azure completes rollback. Closing pager handoff to follow-up SRE.
SRE-Oncall: follow-up owner assigned: Luca. Postmortem owner: Priya. Next steps include: collect netflow, BGP dumps, Azure TAC ticket logs, and schedule postmortem with customers.
Priya: thanks everyone. Summary will go to #incidents-postmortems and I'll link the docs. If any re-escalation, ping me directly. (react: :pray:)
